objective: Take up TIME-KNOTS-20261107-001's selected next step (G5, question 4, toward the program's first emergence): two rings, each running a local dynamics, joined through one contact cell whose update reads both. Written as the space-time law of the coupled dynamics and read with K1-K3, which contact laws make the contact's future knot with both rings' pasts, so that every such knot meets both rings (two-sided) at every lag (persistence), and erasing either ring loses it; what changes when the contact also feeds back into the rings, so that their pasts are no longer independent; and whether such a contact passes the contact gate read across time. Knots are read both with the first rows (A30) and in the whole space-time law.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: a contact that listens to two rings binds both at lag T (every minimally decisive set of its future meets both, equivalently forgetting either ring frees it: two-sided essentiality and loss under erasure across time) exactly when it is a parity of two contact cells that still remember their first rows, and between linear rings it persists unless a ring polynomial is nilpotent (rules 0, 255; 60, 102, 90 and negations on 2^k cells); a contact shared by identity feeds the rings back and binds at every lag in only 44 of 128,128 exact configurations, all parities, breaking 13,068 of 13,104 listening bindings and rescuing 8 (one size past: the same, with persistence growing with ring size). Next: shared contacts that do not read themselves (G5, A31).
stop_rule: Stop when the contact laws that bind both rings' pasts are characterized by proof for contacts that only listen, the feedback case is measured on a declared family (elementary ring rules, contact laws of up to three inputs, lags to a declared bound), and each item of the contact gate read across time is decided, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: Knots between processes: a contact binds two processes exactly when it is a parity, and sharing it costs persistence
